experiment: CBMC proof of mechanically extracted deployed RTNN control functions

extraction.method: function bodies mechanically extracted from the deployed core; numerical kernels are nondeterministic stubs only for control-flow and physical run_block call-count proof

actual_budget_lowering.domain: all uint16_t Q0.16 budget pairs b0<=b1

actual_adaptive_physical_call_cap.domain: all uint16_t budgets, all uint8_t deadline classes, all possible entropy continue/stop outcomes
properties: run_block calls remain in canonical nested order
run_block call count never exceeds min(budget ceiling, normalized deadline, policy max exit)
reported executed exit equals physical run_block call count
reported execution never exceeds budget ceiling
deadline values >6 fail closed to zero physical blocks
NULL executed-output pointer does not change canonical block order
NULL executed-output pointer does not bypass the effective physical work cap
class is capped by deployed policy maximum exit 5
certification path calls run_block exactly the normalized class count
blocks execute in canonical nested order

solver_result: all four proof entry points report VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL with unwinding assertions on adaptive/certification loops
nonclaims: Neural numerical kernels are abstracted as nondeterministic stubs; their arithmetic correctness is not proved here.
The entropy threshold value is abstracted because the proof includes every possible continue/stop outcome.
This is source-level control proof and does not prove compiler preservation of the control semantics.
This does not prove Ibex RTL timing or physical FPGA/ASIC/silicon WCET; those are separate evidence layers.
